可以直接以 Armino 的 OTP driver 为主体导入，但不能简单复制一个 `bk_otp_ahb_read()` 函数就结束。

Armino 的真实实现位于：

```text
~/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/otp/otp_driver_v1_1.c
```

核心结构是：

```text
bk_otp_ahb_read(item, buf, size)
  ├─ 检查 item < OTP2_MAX_ID
  ├─ bk_otp_ahb_read_permission(item)
  │   ├─ OTP_ACTIVE(2)
  │   ├─ 读 OTP2 permission
  │   ├─ 读 OTP2 mask
  │   └─ OTP_SLEEP()
  ├─ OTP_ACTIVE(2)
  │   ├─ 选择 OTP2 map
  │   ├─ 初始化 OTP HAL
  │   └─ 激活 OTP controller
  ├─ 检查 size <= otp_map[item].allocated_size
  ├─ 按 32-bit word 读取 otp2_hal_read_otp()
  ├─ 处理 item 的非 4-byte 对齐 offset
  └─ OTP_SLEEP()
```

对应源文件还依赖：

```text
otp_driver_v1_1.c
otp_driver.h
otp_hal.h / OTP HAL 实现
构建生成的 _otp.c          // item → offset / allocated_size map
driver/otp_types.h
```

你说“直接抄他的”，正确的实现方式应该是：

```text
chips/bk7258/otp/
  ├─ authority/
  │   └─ 保留 Armino OTP driver / HAL 原始来源与 provenance
  ├─ bk7258_otp.c
  │   └─ 只适配 NuttX 的：
  │       getreg32/putreg32
  │       spinlock / critical section
  │       delay
  │       BK7258 寄存器基址
  └─ generated/
      └─ 当前选定完整工程产生的 _otp.c / OTP map
```

也就是说，主体应是 Armino 的 `otp_driver_v1_1.c` 逻辑，而不是我此前那种手写的简化读实现。

但现在有一个必须先停住的事实：

```text
Armino 的 otp_driver_v1_1.c 不仅实现 read，
还实现 bk_otp_apb_update() / bk_otp_ahb_update()。
```

这两条 update 路径会：

```text
检查 permission
→ 检查只能 0 → 1，不能 1 → 0
→ otp_write_otp() / otp2_write_otp()
→ 再读回校验
```

即真实烧写 OTP；这是不可逆的。

所以导入时应分两步：

```text
第一步：导入 Armino 的 read / permission / map / activate / sleep 原始逻辑，
        适配 NuttX 和 BK7258 register integration。

第二步：保留 update API 的符号与参数检查，
        但默认禁止进入硬件 write path。
```

这不是“手写 shim 隐藏缺失”，而是明确的安全策略：Wi‑Fi 初始化和读取 factory calibration 不需要烧 OTP；只有用户明确授权工厂烧录/校准持久化时，才应打开真正的 write path。

还有一点需要纠正：我之前在 `otp.h` 注释里引用了 `iperf` 的生成 `_otp.h`，这不符合你刚定下的规则。之后 OTP map 必须来自你指定的完整 SDK `~/armino/bk_avdk_smp` 中**最终选定 project 的实际生成 map**，不能再把 `iperf` 当通用 authority。

因此下一步应是：

```text
从完整 SDK 选定的 BK7258 project build 产物中取它实际生成的 _otp.c/_otp.h
→ 原样导入 Armino OTP driver/HAL 结构
→ 仅适配 NuttX/SoC integration
→ update 硬件烧写路径默认禁用
→ 再开启 CONFIG_OTP_V1
```

是的，保持这种逻辑主体应是 Armino 的 otp_driver_v1_1.c 逻辑 然后适配过来
我会按这个方向实现：保留 Armino `otp_driver_v1_1.c` 的激活、权限检查、按字读取与非对齐拷贝逻辑，只替换 NuttX 的锁、MMIO、延时和构建期 map 接入；OTP 编程路径继续默认拒绝。先核对仓库内现有 authority 导入物和当前 OTP map 来源，避免再把 `iperf` 的生成 map 混进来。

#define OTP_HARDWARE_ACTIVE (UINT32_C(1) << 0 | UINT32_C(1) << 1)

static spinlock_t g_otp_lock = SP_UNLOCKED;

static int bk7258_otp_wait_ready(void)
{
  unsigned int count;
  uint32_t status;

  for (count = 0; count < 10000; count++)
    {
      status = getreg32(OTP_STATUS);
      if ((status & OTP_STATUS_BUSY) == 0)
        {
          return (status & OTP_STATUS_FAILED) == 0 ? OK : -EIO;
        }
      up_udelay(1);
    }

  return -ETIMEDOUT;
}

static int bk7258_otp_activate(void)
{
  int ret;

  modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_DEV_CLK_EN, 0, BK7258_SYS_OTP_CLK_EN);
  up_udelay(10);
  modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_POWER_WAKEUP, BK7258_SYS_ENCP_POWERDOWN, 0);
  up_udelay(10);
  /* Authority otp_ll_active(): pdstb=1 and clkosc_en=1 before every
   * controller read.  Merely releasing ENCP power is insufficient. */
  putreg32(OTP_HARDWARE_ACTIVE, OTP_HARDWARE);
  ret = bk7258_otp_wait_ready();
  if (ret < 0)
    {
      modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_POWER_WAKEUP, 0, BK7258_SYS_ENCP_POWERDOWN);
      modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_DEV_CLK_EN, BK7258_SYS_OTP_CLK_EN, 0);
    }
  return ret;
}

static void bk7258_otp_sleep(void)
{
  (void)bk7258_otp_wait_ready();
  putreg32(0, OTP_HARDWARE);
  modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_POWER_WAKEUP, 0, BK7258_SYS_ENCP_POWERDOWN);
  modifyreg32(BK7258_SYS_DEV_CLK_EN, BK7258_SYS_OTP_CLK_EN, 0);
}

static uint32_t bk7258_otp1_permission(uint32_t word)
{
  uint32_t permission = getreg32(OTP1_PERMISSION + ((word / 8) << 2));
  uint32_t mask = getreg32(OTP1_MASK + ((word / 128) << 2));

  permission = (permission >> ((word % 8) * 4)) & UINT32_C(0xf);
  mask = (mask >> ((word % 128 / 8) * 2)) & UINT32_C(0x3);
  return permission > mask ? permission : mask;
}

static uint32_t bk7258_otp2_permission(uint32_t word)
{
  uint32_t permission = getreg32(OTP2_PERMISSION + ((word / 256) << 2));
  uint32_t mask = getreg32(OTP2_MASK + ((word / 512) << 2));

  permission = (permission >> ((word % 256 / 32) * 4)) & UINT32_C(0xf);
  mask = (mask >> ((word % 512 / 32) * 2)) & UINT32_C(0x3);
  return permission > mask ? permission : mask;
}

static bk_err_t bk7258_otp_read(const struct bk7258_otp_item_s *entry,
                                 bool ahb, uint8_t *buf, uint32_t size)
{
  uintptr_t base = ahb ? BK7258_OTP_AHB_BASE : OTP1_DATA;
  uint32_t word;
  uint32_t start;
  irqstate_t flags;
  int ret;

  if (buf == NULL)
    {
      return BK_ERR_OTP_READ_BUFFER_NULL;
    }
  if (size > entry->size)
    {
      return BK_ERR_OTP_ADDR_OUT_OF_RANGE;
    }

  flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_otp_lock);
  ret = bk7258_otp_activate();
  if (ret < 0)
    {
      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_otp_lock, flags);
      return BK_FAIL;
    }

  word = entry->offset / 4;
  if ((ahb ? bk7258_otp2_permission(word) : bk7258_otp1_permission(word)) >
      OTP_READ_ONLY)
    {
      bk7258_otp_sleep();
      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_otp_lock, flags);
      return BK_ERR_NO_READ_PERMISSION;
    }

  start = entry->offset % 4;
  while (size > 0)
    {
      uint32_t value = getreg32(base + (word << 2));
      uint32_t count = size < 4 - start ? size : 4 - start;
      uint32_t index;

      for (index = 0; index < count; index++)
        {
          *buf++ = (uint8_t)(value >> ((start + index) * 8));
        }
      size -= count;
      word++;
      start = 0;
    }

  bk7258_otp_sleep();
  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_otp_lock, flags);
  return BK_OK;
}

static int switch_map(uint8_t map_id)
{
	if(otp_map == NULL){
		if (map_id == 1) {
			otp_map = otp_map_1;
		} else if (map_id == 2) {
			otp_map = otp_map_2;
		} else {
			return -1;
		}
	} else {
		return -1;
	}
	return 0;
}

#define OTP_ACTIVE(map_id) \
	do { \
		int ret = switch_map(map_id); \
		if(ret != 0) { \
			return ret;\
		} \
		ret = otp_active(); \
		if(ret != 0) { \
			otp_sleep(); \
			otp_map = NULL; \
			return -1;\
		} \
	} while(0);

#define OTP_SLEEP() \
	do { \
		otp_sleep(); \
		otp_map = NULL; \
	} while(0);

/**
 * obtain APB OTP value in little endian with item ID:
 * 1. allowed start address of item not aligned
 * 2. allowed end address of item not aligned
 */
bk_err_t bk_otp_apb_read(otp1_id_t item, uint8_t* buf, uint32_t size)
{
	if (item >= OTP1_MAX_ID) {
		return BK_ERR_OTP_INDEX_WRONG;
	}

	if( bk_otp_apb_read_permission(item) > OTP_READ_ONLY ) {
		return BK_ERR_NO_READ_PERMISSION;
	}
	OTP_ACTIVE(1)
	if(size > otp_map[item].allocated_size){
		OTP_SLEEP()
		return BK_ERR_OTP_ADDR_OUT_OF_RANGE;
	}
	uint32_t location = otp_map[item].offset / 4;
	uint32_t start = otp_map[item].offset % 4;
	uint32_t value;

	while(size > 0) {
		value = otp_read_otp(location);

		uint8_t * src_data = (uint8_t *)&value;
		int       cpy_cnt;

		src_data += start;

		cpy_cnt = (size >= (4 - start)) ? (4 - start) : size;

		switch( cpy_cnt ) {
			case 4:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
			case 3:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
			case 2:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
			case 1:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
		}

		size -= cpy_cnt;
		location++;
		start = 0;
	}
	OTP_SLEEP()
	return BK_OK;
}

/**
 * @brief     OTP read with item real offset
 *
 * @param item_offset the real item offset to read from otp
 * @param buf point to the buffer that reads the data
 * @param size length of item to read

 *    - others: other errors.
 */

{
	OTP_ACTIVE(1)

	while(size > 0) {
		value = otp_read_otp(location);

		cpy_cnt = (size >= (4 - start)) ? (4 - start) : size;

		switch( cpy_cnt ) {
			case 4:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
			case 3:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;

				*buf++ = *src_data++;

/**
 * update APB OTP value in little endian with item ID:
 * 1. allowed start address of item not aligned
 * 2. allowed end address of item not aligned
 * 3. check overwritable before write, return BK_ERR_OTP_CANNOT_WRTIE if failed
 * 4. verify value after write, return BK_ERR_OTP_UPDATE_NOT_EQUAL if failed
 */
bk_err_t bk_otp_apb_update(otp1_id_t item, uint8_t* buf, uint32_t size)
{
	if (item >= OTP1_MAX_ID) {

		return BK_ERR_NO_WRITE_PERMISSION;
	}
	OTP_ACTIVE(1)
	if(size > otp_map[item].allocated_size){
		OTP_SLEEP()
		return BK_ERR_OTP_ADDR_OUT_OF_RANGE;
	}
	uint32_t location = otp_map[item].offset / 4;
	uint32_t start = otp_map[item].offset % 4;
	uint32_t value = 0;

第一层：直接改变 `g_phy_os_funcs` / `g_phy_os_variable` 表内容的宏。

`CONFIG_OTP_V1` 现在已使以下表项有效：

```text

~/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/boards/bk7258/csv/otp2.csv
```

并已验证这两份 CSV 与此前生成 map 内容一致。

`CONFIG_BLUETOOTH` 仍不应直接打开。它会让 PHY adapter 中以下 wrapper 不再返回安全 stub，而改为调用实际 Bluetooth provider：

```text
ble_in_dut_mode()
bluetooth_rf_test_mode_retrig()
get_tx_pwr_idx()
txpwr_max_set_bt_polar()
txpwr_max_set_bt_iq()
```

同时 `g_phy_os_variable._dd_dev_type_ble` 会被填入真实 BLE driver-model ID。当前本地没有完整 Bluetooth/coex provider，因此只改成 `1` 会变成链接或运行期假对齐。

第二层：不直接改变 PHY 表布局，但决定 PHY 表回调后能否走完整工程同样的多核路径。这是当前最重要的未对齐域：

| 项目 | 完整 SDK BK7258 | 本地 | 为什么不能只改宏 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `CONFIG_CPU_CNT` | `3` | 未定义，实际按单核处理 | 会启用 PHY/SARADC server 与多核协作分支 |
| `CONFIG_PHY_MB` | Kconfig 默认 `y` | `0` | 会让 `bk_sensor_init()` 初始化 PHY mailbox，并在多核时启动 PHY server |
| `CONFIG_SARADC_MB` | `y` | 未定义/未启用 | 会让 SARADC 进入 mailbox 协调路径 |
| `CONFIG_MAILBOX` / IPC 语义 | 完整 Armino mailbox v2 | NuttX mailbox 已有，但非同一 server 协议 | 需要验证 channel、消息、ack、生命周期等价 |

这三个必须作为一个整体处理：

```text
CPU_CNT=3
→ PHY_MB=1
→ SARADC_MB=1
→ Armino-compatible PHY/SARADC mailbox channel
→ PHY/SARADC server lifecycle
```

不能先单独改：

```c
#define CONFIG_CPU_CNT 3
#define CONFIG_PHY_MB 1
#define CONFIG_SARADC_MB 1
```

因为完整 SDK 的对应路径会要求：

```text
mb_phy_ipc_init()
bk_phy_server_init()
mb_saradc_ipc_init()
bk_saradc_server_init()
```

当前本地虽然已有 `bk7258_pm_ipc_phy_init()` / `bk7258_pm_ipc_saradc_init()` 方向的适配接口，但还没有证据证明完整的 Armino server 生命周期已经存在并等价。因此这仍是当前 PHY calibration 前置环境最大的配置缺口。

第三层：不属于 `g_phy_os_funcs` 表的直接字段，但会影响 PHY/RF 实际运行环境。

| 项目 | 完整 SDK BK7258 | 当前本地 | 风险 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `CONFIG_WIFI_VNET_CONTROLLER` | `y` | `0` | 影响 `wifi_init()` 末尾 `cif_init()`；不解释当前 calibration，但完整 Wi‑Fi 后段不等价 |
| `CONFIG_CKMN` | `y` | 未启用 | 本地 RC32K ppm provider 当前仅返回 `0`，不是真实 clock-monitor 行为 |
| `CONFIG_AON_RTC` | `y` | 未完整对齐 | 影响 tick/LPO/时间来源的完整性 |
| `CONFIG_PSRAM` | `y` | NuttX 有 PSRAM，但非 Armino 完整 provider 域 | 影响 heap/缓冲区/某些 vendor 条件路径 |
| `CONFIG_AON_PMU` | `y` | callback 已有 BK7258 provider | 表内容不受此宏直接控制，但 PMU 读取行为仍需板上验证 |
| `CONFIG_VND_CAL` | `y` | runtime 已调用 `vnd_cal_overlay()` | 行为层部分已补；宏与完整工程仍没有统一管理 |
| `CONFIG_PHY_RFCALI_TO_OTP` | `n` | 未定义，行为等效为关闭 | 已对齐；绝不能开启 |

所以当前状态可以概括为：

```text
PHY adapter ABI / SoC family：
  基本已对齐。

OTP calibration read：
  已对齐到完整 SDK 的 BK7258 board map 和 Armino read lifecycle。

Bluetooth/coex：
  未对齐，且当前不应只开宏。

PHY/SARADC mailbox + CPU_CNT=3：
  未对齐，是下一组真正需要实现的核心缺口。

VNET / CKMN / AON RTC / PSRAM：
 仍有运行域差异，但不是当前校准第一优先级。
```

下一步最合理的是先处理这一组，而不是继续散改 config：

```text
CONFIG_CPU_CNT=3
CONFIG_PHY_MB=1
CONFIG_SARADC_MB=1
```

```text
  → 真实不可逆烧写
```

因此有两个不同的目标，不能混称“对齐”：

```text
A. Wi‑Fi 当前正常运行所需的 profile
   CONFIG_PHY_RFCALI_TO_OTP=n
   → 正常校准不应请求写 OTP
   → 读取 OTP/校准数据必须与 Armino 一致

B. 连 OTP 烧写 API 被外部主动调用时也要逐项完全一致
   → 必须导入原厂 write/update 行为
   → 会让固件具备不可逆烧写能力
```

我建议的方案是：

```text

- 写入侧：不自创“安全拒绝”等价物，也不把它称为 Armino 等价。
- 是否导入并启用原厂真正 write path：
  必须由你明确确认，因为这会让运行中的固件具备不可逆烧写 OTP 的能力。
```

这是高风险动作：即使 `CONFIG_PHY_RFCALI_TO_OTP=n`，错误调用或以后配置变化也可能触发写入。因此我不会自行把原厂烧写路径放入可运行镜像。

它们共享 PHY/RF，所以不是“Wi‑Fi 不需要蓝牙就可以把 `CONFIG_BLUETOOTH` 当无关宏”。开启 Bluetooth 后，`g_phy_os_funcs` 的以下 callback 会从当前 stub 切换到真实 BT provider：

```text

_get_tx_pwr_idx
_txpwr_max_set_bt_polar
_ble_tx_testmode_retrig
_txpwr_max_set_bt_iq
_get_ble_polar_mode
```

并且：

```text

```

会从零值变成 Armino 的 `DD_DEV_TYPE_BLE`。

但当前 Vela/NuttX 没有完整 Armino Bluetooth/coex provider。故结论不是“现在直接打开”，而是：

```text
Wi‑Fi-only runtime profile：
  可以暂时保持 CONFIG_BLUETOOTH=0；
 这是明确、受控的 profile 差异。

完整 BK7258 profile：
  必须导入/适配 Bluetooth + BLE + RF coexist provider；
  然后再打开 CONFIG_BLUETOOTH=1。
```

`wifi_init()` 中 `coex_init()` 被 `#if 0` 编译排除，不代表不存在 RF 共存依赖：Bluetooth 和 Wi‑Fi 仍通过 RF vote、PHY table、BT callback、功率/校准配置共享同一 RF 域。

因此，蓝牙不是当前 `idx:40` 校准卡点的第一优先级，但它是“完整配置一致”的独立工作包，不能靠改一个宏完成。

## CPU_CNT / PHY_MB / SARADC_MB：是否要基于 Vela RPMsg 改造

是，但不能把 Armino mailbox v2 简单替换成“发一条 RPMsg”就认为完成。

Armino 的关系是：

```text
CONFIG_CPU_CNT=3
  → CONFIG_MAILBOX / CONFIG_MAILBOX_IPC
  → CONFIG_PHY_MB
      → mb_phy_ipc_init()
      → bk_phy_server_init()
  → CONFIG_SARADC_MB
      → mb_saradc_ipc_init()
      → bk_saradc_server_init()
  → bk_pm_mailbox_init()
```

这些并不只是数据传输；它们定义了：

```text
- 哪个核处理 PHY/SARADC 请求
- 请求/确认的消息格式
- channel ID
- ACK/完成时序
- server 的线程或任务生命周期
- PM power/clock vote 在哪个核执行
- 超时和错误语义
```

Vela 的 RPMsg/RPTUN 可以承担**传输层**，但必须在其上实现 Armino 的 mailbox 语义：

```text
Armino PHY/SARADC mailbox semantic adapter
  ├─ 编码 authority 的 channel / operation / request / ack
  ├─ 映射到 BK7258 NuttX mailbox + RPMsg/RPTUN
  ├─ 实现 server 初始化与回调分发
  ├─ 保持同步/异步、超时、返回码语义
  └─ 验证 remote CPU/AP 侧真的有对应服务
```

不能这样做：

```c
#define CONFIG_CPU_CNT 3
#define CONFIG_PHY_MB 1
#define CONFIG_SARADC_MB 1
```

然后让 `mb_phy_ipc_init()` 或 `bk_phy_server_init()` 返回成功。

这样闭源 PHY/SARADC 会进入多核路径，却等不到 authority 期待的 server/ack，最可能出现的症状就是校准、温度、电压或 PM 操作静默卡住。

### 多核/IPC 的实施顺序

```text
1. 固定 Armino mailbox contract
   - 导入 authority 的 bk_phy_notify.c / saradc_notify.c
   - 固定每个 channel、opcode、payload、ack 和 timeout
   - 固定 CPU0/CPU1/CPU2 的职责

2. 审计本地 BK7258 mailbox/RPMsg 能力
   - 现有 bk7258_mailbox.c
   - 现有 bk7258_pm_ipc.c
   - RPTUN endpoint 生命周期
   - AP 是否已经运行匹配服务

3. 实现 PHY service
   mb_phy_ipc_init()
   bk_phy_server_init()
   mb_phy_op_prepare()
   mb_phy_op_finish()

4. 实现 SARADC service
   mb_saradc_ipc_init()
   bk_saradc_server_init()
   mb_saradc_op_prepare()
   mb_saradc_op_finish()

5. 用 host/board probes 验证
   request → remote handler → ack → return code
   而不是只验证“调用未报错”

6. 最后才一起打开：
   CONFIG_CPU_CNT=3
   CONFIG_PHY_MB=1
   CONFIG_SARADC_MB=1
```

这里的关键决策是：

```text
如果 Vela AP/CPU1/CPU2 没有对应 Armino-equivalent PHY/SARADC service，
就不能开启 CPU_CNT=3 的 authority 多核业务路径。

如果 AP 已能启动并提供该服务，
则以 RPMsg 为 transport、以 Armino mailbox protocol 为 semantic contract。
```

    65	static bk_err_t send_saradc_op_state(uint8_t state)
    66	{
    67		uint64_t us_start = 0;
    68		uint64_t us_end = 0;
    69	
    70		saradc_erase_ipc_state = IPC_SARADC_OP_REQ;
    71	
    72		mb_chnl_cmd_t  cmd_buf;
    73	
    74		cmd_buf.hdr.data = 0; /* clear hdr. */
    75		cmd_buf.hdr.cmd  = state;
    76		cmd_buf.param1 = saradc_erase_ipc_state;
    77	
    78		bk_err_t   ret_val = mb_chnl_write(MB_CHNL_SARADC, &cmd_buf);
    79	
    80		if(ret_val != BK_OK)
    81			return ret_val;
    82	
    83		us_start = bk_aon_rtc_get_us();
    84	
    85		for(int i = 0; i < 2000; i++)
    86		{
    87			if(saradc_erase_ipc_state == IPC_SARADC_OP_ACK)
    88			{
    89				break;
    90			}
    91	
    92			us_end = bk_aon_rtc_get_us();
    93			// wait ack time should not be more than 5 ms
    94			if((us_end - us_start) > SARADC_WAIT_ACK_TIMEOUT)
    95			{
    96				return BK_FAIL;
    97			}
    98		}
    99	
   100		return BK_OK;
   101	}

    48	static uint32_t calc_crc32(uint32_t crc, const uint8_t *buf, int len)
    49	{
    50	    uint8_t i;
    51	
    52	    while (len--) {
    53	        crc ^= *buf++;
    54	        for (i = 8; i > 0; i--) {
    55	            if (crc & 0x80) {
    56	                crc = (crc << 1) ^ 0x31;
    57	            } else {
    58	                crc <<= 1;
    59	            }
    60	        }
    61	    }
    62	
    63	    return crc;
    64	}

   123	static void phy_cmd_handler(u32 handle, u8 connect_id)
   124	{
   125		phy_cmd_t cmd_buff;
   126		int recv_len = mb_ipc_get_recv_data_len(handle);
   127		u8 user_cmd = INVALID_USER_CMD_ID;
   128	
   129		memset(&cmd_buff, 0, sizeof(phy_cmd_t));
   130	
   131		if(recv_len != sizeof(phy_cmd_t))
   132		{
   133			mb_ipc_recv(handle, &user_cmd, NULL, 0, 0);
   134	
   135			// if client wait_forever, then must send a response even if user_cmd == INVALID_USER_CMD_ID.
   136			// flash client does not wait forever, so only respond then cmd is valid.
   137			if(user_cmd != INVALID_USER_CMD_ID)
   138				phy_error_handler(handle, user_cmd);
   139	
   140			TRACE_I(TAG, "recv user_cmd=%d, data len failed! %d,cmd_buff_size=%d\r\n", user_cmd, recv_len,sizeof(phy_cmd_t));
   141	
   142			return;
   143		}
   144	
   145		recv_len = mb_ipc_recv(handle, &user_cmd, (u8 *)&cmd_buff, sizeof(phy_cmd_t), 0);
   146	
   147		if(recv_len != sizeof(phy_cmd_t))
   148		{
   149			// if client wait_forever, then must send a response even if user_cmd == INVALID_USER_CMD_ID.
   150			// flash client does not wait forever, so only respond then cmd is valid.
   151			if(user_cmd != INVALID_USER_CMD_ID)
   152				phy_error_handler(handle, user_cmd);
   153	
   154			TRACE_I(TAG, "recv user_cmd=%d, data len failed! %d,cmd_buff_size=%d\r\n", user_cmd, recv_len,sizeof(phy_cmd_t));
   155	
   156			return;
   157		}
   158	
   159		switch(user_cmd)
   160		{
   161			case PHY_CMD_GET_TEMP:
   162				bk_phy_get_current_temperature_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   163				break;
   164			case PHY_CMD_GET_VOLT:
   165				bk_phy_get_current_voltage_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   166				break;
   167			case PHY_CMD_GET_MAC_ADDR:
   168				bk_phy_get_mac_addr_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   169				break;
   170			case PHY_CMD_GET_STA_MAC_ADDR:
   171				bk_phy_wifi_sta_get_mac_addr_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   172				break;
   173			case PHY_CMD_GET_AP_MAC_ADDR:
   174				bk_phy_wifi_ap_get_mac_addr_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   175				break;
   176			case PHY_CMD_SET_MAC_ADDR:
   177				bk_phy_set_mac_addr_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   178				break;
   179			default:
   180				phy_error_handler(handle, user_cmd);
   181				TRACE_I(TAG, "0x%x, unknown cmd%d!\r\n", handle, user_cmd);
   182				break;
   183		}
   184	}

   186	static void phy_svr_connect_handler(u32 handle, u8 connect_id)
   187	{
   188		u32  cmd_id;
   189	
   190		int ret_val = mb_ipc_get_recv_event(handle, &cmd_id);
   191	
   192		if(ret_val != 0)  // failed
   193		{
   194			TRACE_I(TAG, "get evt fail %x %d.\r\n", handle, ret_val);
   195			return;
   196		}
   197	
   198		if(cmd_id > MB_IPC_CMD_MAX)
   199		{
   200			TRACE_I(TAG, "cmd-id error %d.\r\n", cmd_id);
   201			return;
   202		}
   203	
   204		u8  src =0, dst = 0;
   205	
   206		extern int mb_ipc_get_connection(u32 handle, u8 *src, u8 * dst);
   207	
   208		mb_ipc_get_connection(handle, &src, &dst);
   209	
   210		if(cmd_id == MB_IPC_SEND_CMD)
   211		{
   212			phy_cmd_handler(handle, connect_id);
   213		}
   214		else  /* any other commands. */
   215		{
   216			TRACE_I(TAG, "cmd=%d, 0x%x, %x-%x.\r\n", cmd_id, handle, src, dst);
   217		}
   218	}

   225	static u32 phy_svr_rx_callback(u32 handle, u32 connect_id)
   226	{
   227		u32  connect_flag;
   228	
   229		if(connect_id >= PHY_SVR_CONNECT_MAX)
   230			return 0;
   231	
   232		connect_flag = 0x01 << connect_id;
   233	
   234		rtos_set_event_ex(&phy_svr_event, connect_flag);
   235	
   236		return 0;
   237	}
   238	
   239	static void phy_svr_task(void *param)
   240	{
   241		u32 event;
   242		u32  handle;
   243		u32  connect_handle;
   244	
   245		if(rtos_init_event_ex(&phy_svr_event) != BK_OK)
   246		{
   247			rtos_delete_thread(NULL);
   248			return;
   249		}
   250	
   251		handle = mb_ipc_socket(IPC_GET_ID_PORT(PHY_SERVER), phy_svr_rx_callback);
   252	
   253		if(handle == 0)
   254		{
   255			TRACE_I("ipc_svr", "create_socket failed.\r\n");
   256	
   257			rtos_deinit_event_ex(&phy_svr_event);
   258			rtos_delete_thread(NULL);
   259	
   260			return ;
   261		}
   262	
   263		s_phy_svr_init = 2;
   264	
   265		while(1)
   266		{
   267			event = rtos_wait_event_ex(&phy_svr_event, PHY_SVR_EVENTS, 1, BEKEN_WAIT_FOREVER);
   268	
   269			if(event == 0)  // timeout.
   270			{
   271				continue;
   272			}
   273	
   274			if(event & PHY_SVR_QUIT_EVENT)
   275			{
   276				TRACE_I(TAG, "saradc server task quit\r\n");
   277				break;
   278			}
   279	
   280			// Handle connection events
   281			for(int i = 0; i < PHY_SVR_CONNECT_MAX; i++)
   282			{
   283				if(event & (0x01 << i))
   284				{
   285					connect_handle = mb_ipc_server_get_connect_handle(handle, i);
   286					phy_svr_connect_handler(connect_handle, i);
   287				}
   288			}
   289		}
   290		mb_ipc_server_close(handle, PHY_SVR_WAIT_TIME);
   291		rtos_deinit_event_ex(&phy_svr_event);
   292		s_phy_svr_init = 0;
   293		rtos_delete_thread(NULL);
   294	}

    50	static uint32_t calc_crc32(uint32_t crc, const uint8_t *buf, int len)
    51	{
    52	    uint8_t i;
    53	
    54	    while (len--) {
    55	        crc ^= *buf++;
    56	        for (i = 8; i > 0; i--) {
    57	            if (crc & 0x80) {
    58	                crc = (crc << 1) ^ 0x31;
    59	            } else {
    60	                crc <<= 1;
    61	            }
    62	        }
    63	    }
    64	
    65	    return crc;
    66	}

   109	static void saradc_read_raw_handler(u32 handle, saradc_cmd_t *cmd_buff, u8 connect_id)
   110	{
   111		int read_status = BK_OK;
   112		u16 *read_buff = saradc_buff;
   113	
   114		if(cmd_buff->size > sizeof(saradc_buff))
   115		{
   116			saradc_error_handler(handle, SARADC_CMD_READ_RAW);
   117			TRACE_I(TAG, "%s @%d, 0x%x buffer overflow!\r\n", __FUNCTION__, __LINE__, handle);
   118			return;
   119		}
   120	
   121		read_status = bk_adc_read_raw(read_buff, cmd_buff->size, cmd_buff->timeout);
   122	
   123		cmd_buff->ret_status = read_status;
   124		//cmd_buff->buff = read_buff;
   125		memcpy(cmd_buff->buff, read_buff, cmd_buff->size * sizeof(u16));
   126	
   127		cmd_buff->crc = calc_crc32(0, (UINT8 *)read_buff, cmd_buff->size * sizeof(uint16_t));
   128	
   129		int ret_val = mb_ipc_send(handle, SARADC_CMD_READ_RAW, (u8 *)cmd_buff, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t), SARADC_SVR_WAIT_TIME);
   130	
   131		if(read_status != BK_OK)
   132		{
   133			TRACE_I(TAG, "%s @%d, 0x%x read failed!\r\n", __FUNCTION__, __LINE__, handle);
   134			return;
   135		}
   136	
   137		if(ret_val != 0)
   138		{
   139			(*read_buff) ^= 0x01;   // make crc not match
   140			TRACE_I(TAG, "%s @%d, 0x%x send failed, ret_val = %d!\r\n", __FUNCTION__, __LINE__, handle, ret_val);
   141			return;
   142		}
   143	
   144		u32 event = rtos_wait_event_ex(&saradc_svr_event, (0x01 << connect_id), 1, SARADC_SVR_WAIT_TIME);
   145	
   146		if(event == 0)
   147		{
   148			(*read_buff) ^= 0x01;   // make crc not match
   149			TRACE_I(TAG, "%s @%d, 0x%x read done failed!\r\n", __FUNCTION__, __LINE__, handle);
   150			return;
   151		}
   152	
   153		memset(cmd_buff, 0, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t));
   154		u8 user_cmd = INVALID_USER_CMD_ID;
   155		ret_val = mb_ipc_recv(handle, &user_cmd, (u8 *)cmd_buff, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t), SARADC_SVR_WAIT_TIME);
   156	
   157		if((ret_val != sizeof(saradc_cmd_t)) || (user_cmd != SARADC_CMD_READ_RAW_DONE))
   158		{
   159			TRACE_I(TAG, "%s @%d, 0x%x recv cmd%d, %d, 0x%x!\r\n", __FUNCTION__, __LINE__, handle, user_cmd, ret_val, event);
   160		}
   161		else
   162		{
   163			memset(cmd_buff, 0, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t));
   164			cmd_buff->ret_status = BK_OK;
   165			mb_ipc_send(handle, SARADC_CMD_READ_RAW_DONE, (u8 *)cmd_buff, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t), SARADC_SVR_WAIT_TIME);
   166		}
   167	}

   169	static void saradc_read_handler(u32 handle, saradc_cmd_t *cmd_buff, u8 connect_id)
   170	{
   171		int read_status = BK_OK;
   172		uint16_t read_buff = 0;
   173	
   174		if(cmd_buff->size > sizeof(saradc_buff))
   175		{
   176			saradc_error_handler(handle, SARADC_CMD_READ);
   177			TRACE_I(TAG, "%s @%d, 0x%x buffer overflow!\r\n", __FUNCTION__, __LINE__, handle);
   178			return;
   179		}
   180	
   181		read_status = bk_adc_read(&read_buff, cmd_buff->timeout);
   182		cmd_buff->ret_status = read_status;
   183		cmd_buff->buff[0] = read_buff;
   184		cmd_buff->crc = calc_crc32(0, (UINT8 *)&read_buff, sizeof(uint16_t));
   185	
   186		int ret_val = mb_ipc_send(handle, SARADC_CMD_READ, (u8 *)cmd_buff, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t), SARADC_SVR_WAIT_TIME);
   187	
   188		if(read_status != BK_OK)
   189		{
   190			TRACE_I(TAG, "%s @%d, 0x%x read failed!\r\n", __FUNCTION__, __LINE__, handle);
   191			return;
   192		}
   193	
   194		if(ret_val != 0)
   195		{
   196			(read_buff) ^= 0x01;   // make crc not match
   197			TRACE_I(TAG, "%s @%d, 0x%x send failed, ret_val = %d!\r\n", __FUNCTION__, __LINE__, handle, ret_val);
   198			return;
   199		}
   200	
   201		u32 event = rtos_wait_event_ex(&saradc_svr_event, (0x01 << connect_id), 1, SARADC_SVR_WAIT_TIME);
   202	
   203		if(event == 0)
   204		{
   205			(read_buff) ^= 0x01;   // make crc not match
   206			TRACE_I(TAG, "%s @%d, 0x%x read done failed!\r\n", __FUNCTION__, __LINE__, handle);
   207			return;
   208		}
   209	
   210		memset(cmd_buff, 0, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t));
   211		u8 user_cmd = INVALID_USER_CMD_ID;
   212		ret_val = mb_ipc_recv(handle, &user_cmd, (u8 *)cmd_buff, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t), SARADC_SVR_WAIT_TIME);
   213	
   214		if((ret_val != sizeof(saradc_cmd_t)) || (user_cmd != SARADC_CMD_READ_DONE))
   215		{
   216			TRACE_I(TAG, "%s @%d, 0x%x recv12121 cmd%d, %d, 0x%x!\r\n", __FUNCTION__, __LINE__, handle, user_cmd, ret_val, event);
   217		}
   218		else
   219		{
   220			memset(cmd_buff, 0, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t));
   221			cmd_buff->ret_status = BK_OK;
   222			mb_ipc_send(handle, SARADC_CMD_READ_DONE, (u8 *)cmd_buff, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t), SARADC_SVR_WAIT_TIME);
   223		}
   224	}

   302	static void saradc_cmd_handler(u32 handle, u8 connect_id)
   303	{
   304		saradc_cmd_t cmd_buff;
   305		int recv_len = mb_ipc_get_recv_data_len(handle);
   306		u8 user_cmd = INVALID_USER_CMD_ID;
   307	
   308		memset(&cmd_buff, 0, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t));
   309	
   310		if(recv_len != sizeof(saradc_cmd_t))
   311		{
   312			mb_ipc_recv(handle, &user_cmd, NULL, 0, 0);  // data_buff == NULL or buff_len == 0 just discard all data.
   313	
   314			// if client wait_forever, then must send a response even if user_cmd == INVALID_USER_CMD_ID.
   315			// flash client does not wait forever, so only respond then cmd is valid.
   316			if(user_cmd != INVALID_USER_CMD_ID)
   317				saradc_error_handler(handle, user_cmd);
   318	
   319			TRACE_I(TAG, "recv user_cmd=%d, data len failed! %d,cmd_buff_size=%d\r\n", user_cmd, recv_len,sizeof(saradc_cmd_t));
   320	
   321			return;
   322		}
   323	
   324		recv_len = mb_ipc_recv(handle, &user_cmd, (u8 *)&cmd_buff, sizeof(saradc_cmd_t), 0);
   325	
   326		if(recv_len != sizeof(saradc_cmd_t))
   327		{
   328			// if client wait_forever, then must send a response even if user_cmd == INVALID_USER_CMD_ID.
   329			// flash client does not wait forever, so only respond then cmd is valid.
   330			if(user_cmd != INVALID_USER_CMD_ID)
   331				saradc_error_handler(handle, user_cmd);
   332	
   333			TRACE_I(TAG, "recv user_cmd=%d, data len failed! %d,cmd_buff_size=%d\r\n", user_cmd, recv_len,sizeof(saradc_cmd_t));
   334	
   335			return;
   336		}
   337	
   338		switch(user_cmd)
   339		{
   340			case SARADC_CMD_ACQUIRE:
   341				saradc_acquire_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   342				break;
   343	
   344			case SARADC_CMD_INIT:
   345				saradc_init_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   346				break;
   347	
   348			case SARADC_CMD_ENABLE_BYPASS_CALIBRATION:
   349				saradc_enable_bypass_calibration_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   350				break;
   351	
   352			case SARADC_CMD_START:
   353				saradc_start_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   354				break;
   355	
   356			case SARADC_CMD_READ_RAW:
   357				saradc_read_raw_handler(handle, &cmd_buff, connect_id);
   358				break;
   359	
   360			case SARADC_CMD_READ:
   361				saradc_read_handler(handle, &cmd_buff, connect_id);
   362				break;
   363	
   364			case SARADC_CMD_STOP:
   365				saradc_stop_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   366				break;
   367	
   368			case SARADC_CMD_DEINIT:
   369				saradc_deinit_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   370				break;
   371	
   372			case SARADC_CMD_RELEASE:
   373				saradc_release_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   374				break;
   375	
   376			case SARADC_CMD_SET_CONFIG:
   377				saradc_set_config_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   378				break;
   379	
   380			case SARADC_CMD_EN:
   381				saradc_en_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   382				break;
   383	
   384			case SARADC_CMD_DATA_CALCULATE:
   385				saradc_data_calculate_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   386				break;
   387	
   388			case SARADC_CMD_INIT_GPIO:
   389				saradc_chan_init_gpio_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   390				break;
   391	
   392			case SARADC_CMD_DEINIT_GPIO:
   393				saradc_chan_deinit_gpio_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   394				break;
   395	
   396			case SARADC_CMD_SET_CHANNEL:
   397				saradc_set_chan_handler(handle, &cmd_buff);
   398				break;
   399	
   400			default:
   401				saradc_error_handler(handle, user_cmd);
   402				TRACE_I(TAG, "0x%x, unknown cmd%d!\r\n", handle, user_cmd);
   403				break;
   404		}
   405	}

   407	static void saradc_svr_connect_handler(u32 handle, u8 connect_id)
   408	{
   409		u32  cmd_id;
   410	
   411		int ret_val = mb_ipc_get_recv_event(handle, &cmd_id);
   412	
   413		if(ret_val != 0)  // failed
   414		{
   415			TRACE_I(TAG, "get evt fail %x %d.\r\n", handle, ret_val);
   416			return;
   417		}
   418	
   419		if(cmd_id > MB_IPC_CMD_MAX)
   420		{
   421			TRACE_I(TAG, "cmd-id error %d.\r\n", cmd_id);
   422			return;
   423		}
   424	
   425		u8  src =0, dst = 0;
   426	
   427		extern int mb_ipc_get_connection(u32 handle, u8 *src, u8 * dst);
   428	
   429		mb_ipc_get_connection(handle, &src, &dst);
   430	
   431		if(cmd_id == MB_IPC_SEND_CMD)
   432		{
   433			bk_pm_module_vote_sleep_ctrl(PM_SLEEP_MODULE_NAME_SARADC,0x0,0x0);
   434			saradc_cmd_handler(handle, connect_id);
   435			bk_pm_module_vote_sleep_ctrl(PM_SLEEP_MODULE_NAME_SARADC,0x1,0x0);
   436		}
   437		else  /* any other commands. */
   438		{
   439			TRACE_I(TAG, "cmd=%d, 0x%x, %x-%x.\r\n", cmd_id, handle, src, dst);
   440		}
   441	}

   448	static u32 saradc_svr_rx_callback(u32 handle, u32 connect_id)
   449	{
   450		u32  connect_flag;
   451	
   452		if(connect_id >= SARADC_SVR_CONNECT_MAX)
   453			return 0;
   454	
   455		connect_flag = 0x01 << connect_id;
   456	
   457		rtos_set_event_ex(&saradc_svr_event, connect_flag);
   458	
   459		return 0;

   198	              BK7258_MBOX_CH_INT_ENABLE);
   199	  /* Discard stale entries before the IRQ is attached.  They belong to an
   200	   * earlier boot and must not be reported as live Mailbox delivery.
   201	   */
   202	
   203	  bk7258_mbox_drain(false);
   204	
   205	  ret = irq_attach(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX, bk7258_mbox_interrupt, NULL);
   206	  if (ret < 0)
   207	    {
   208	      return ret;
   209	    }
   210	
   211	  up_prioritize_irq(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX,
   212	                    CONFIG_BK7258_MAILBOX_IRQ_PRIORITY);
   213	  bk7258_mbox_route_irq();
   214	  up_enable_irq(BK7258_IRQ_MAILBOX);
   215	  g_bk7258_mbox_initialized = true;
   216	  return 0;
   217	}
   218	
   219	int bk7258_mbox_notify(int dst_cpu, uint32_t token)
   220	{
   221	  return bk7258_mbox_notify_magic(dst_cpu, token, BK7258_MBOX_RPTUN_MAGIC);
   222	}
   223	
   224	int bk7258_mbox_notify_magic(int dst_cpu, uint32_t token, uint32_t magic)
   225	{
   226	  unsigned int channel = BK7258_MBOX_LOCAL_CPU;
   227	  irqstate_t flags;
   228	
   229	  if (!g_bk7258_mbox_initialized)
   230	    {
   231	      return -ENODEV;
   232	    }
   233	
   234	  if (dst_cpu < 0 || dst_cpu >= BK7258_MBOX_CHANNELS ||
   235	      dst_cpu == BK7258_MBOX_LOCAL_CPU)
   236	    {
   237	      return -EINVAL;
   238	    }
   239	
   240	  flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&g_bk7258_mbox_lock);
   241	  if ((getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH_FSTAT(dst_cpu)) &
   242	       BK7258_MBOX_FIFO_FULL) != 0)
   243	    {
   244	      spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_mbox_lock, flags);
   245	      return -EBUSY;
   246	    }
   247	
   248	  __asm__ volatile ("dmb" : : : "memory");
   249	  putreg32(token, BK7258_MBOX_CH_TDATA0(channel));
   250	  putreg32(magic, BK7258_MBOX_CH_TDATA1(channel));
   251	  putreg32((uint32_t)dst_cpu, BK7258_MBOX_CH_TID(channel));
   252	  spin_unlock_irqrestore(&g_bk7258_mbox_lock, flags);
   253	  return 0;
   254	}

  "OTP local complete": "     1	/****************************************************************************
     2	 * chips/bk7258/otp/bk7258_otp.c
     3	 *
     4	 * BK7258 OTP/eFuse calibration ABI ownership.
     5	 *
     6	 * The read-side control flow is ported from the BK7258 Armino authority
     7	 * middleware/driver/otp/otp_driver_v1_1.c:
     8	 *
     9	 *   switch_map() -> OTP_ACTIVE() -> permission/mask -> OTP_SLEEP()
    10	 *   -> switch_map() -> OTP_ACTIVE() -> word reads -> OTP_SLEEP()
    11	 *
    12	 * The NuttX integration below substitutes the authority OTP HAL with the
    13	 * equivalent BK7258 MMIO operations and serializes each active window with a
    14	 * NuttX spinlock. Programming remains refused: no runtime Wi-Fi path needs it
    15	 * and OTP programming is irreversible.
    16	 ****************************************************************************/
    17	
    18	#include <nuttx/config.h>
    19	
    20	#include <errno.h>
    21	#include <stdbool.h>
    22	#include <stdint.h>
    23	
    24	#include <common/bk_err.h>
    25	#include <components/log.h>
    26	#include <nuttx/spinlock.h>
    27	
    28	#include <arm_internal.h>
    29	#include <bk7258_memorymap.h>
    30	#include <driver/efuse.h>
    31	#include <driver/otp.h>
    32	
    33	#include "bk7258_otp_map.h"
    34	
    35	#define OTP_TAG "BK7258 OTP"
    36	
    37	#define BK_ERR_OTP_READ_BUFFER_NULL  (BK_ERR_OTP_BASE - 1)
    38	#define BK_ERR_OTP_ADDR_OUT_OF_RANGE (BK_ERR_OTP_BASE - 2)
    39	#define BK_ERR_NO_READ_PERMISSION    (BK_ERR_OTP_BASE - 3)
    40	#define BK_ERR_OTP_INDEX_WRONG       (BK_ERR_OTP_BASE - 14)
    41	
    42	#define OTP_STATUS        (BK7258_OTP_APB_BASE + UINT32_C(0x2c4))
    43	#define OTP_HARDWARE      (BK7258_OTP_APB_BASE + UINT32_C(0x2c8))
    44	#define OTP1_PERMISSION   (BK7258_OTP_APB_BASE + UINT32_C(0x080))
    45	#define OTP1_MASK         (BK7258_OTP_APB_BASE + UINT32_C(0x2b4))
    46	#define OTP2_PERMISSION   (BK7258_OTP_APB_BASE + UINT32_C(0x010))
    47	#define OTP2_MASK         (BK7258_OTP_APB_BASE + UINT32_C(0x280))
    48	#define OTP1_DATA         (BK7258_OTP_APB_BASE + UINT32_C(0x400))
    49	
    50	#define OTP_STATUS_BUSY   UINT32_C(1)
    51	#define OTP_STATUS_FAILED UINT32_C(0x1e)
    52	#define OTP_READ_ONLY     UINT32_C(3)
    53	#define OTP_HARDWARE_ACTIVE (UINT32_C(1) << 0 | UINT32_C(1) << 1)
    54	
    55	static spinlock_t g_otp_lock = SP_UNLOCKED;
    56	static const struct bk7258_otp_item_s *g_otp_map;
    57	static size_t g_otp_map_count;
    58	
    59	/* Authority otp_driver_v1_1.c uses one transient global otp_map selected by
    60	 * OTP_ACTIVE(map_id), then clears it in OTP_SLEEP(). Keep that lifecycle: it
    61	 * is part of the driver's map/permission contract, rather than treating the
    62	 * two OTP address spaces as interchangeable arrays. */
    63	
    64	static int bk7258_otp_switch_map(unsigned int map_id)
    65	{
    66	  if (g_otp_map != NULL)
    67	    {
    68	      return -EBUSY;
    69	    }
    70	
    71	  if (map_id == 1)
    72	    {
    73	      g_otp_map = g_bk7258_otp1_map;
    74	      g_otp_map_count = BK7258_OTP1_ITEMS;
    75	      return OK;
    76	    }
    77	
    78	  if (map_id == 2)
    79	    {
    80	      g_otp_map = g_bk7258_otp2_map;
    81	      g_otp_map_count = BK7258_OTP2_ITEMS;
    82	      return OK;
    83	    }
    84	
    85	  return -EINVAL;
    86	}
    87	static int bk7258_otp_wait_ready(void)
    88	{
    89	  unsigned int count;
    90	  uint32_t status;
    91	
    92	  for (count = 0; count < 10000; count++)
    93	    {
    94	      status = getreg32(OTP_STATUS);
    95	      if ((status & OTP_STATUS_BUSY) == 0)
    96	        {
    97	          return (status & OTP_STATUS_FAILED) == 0 ? OK : -EIO;
    98	        }
    99	      up_udelay(1);
   100	    }
   101	
   102	  return -ETIMEDOUT;
   103	}

   105	static int bk7258_otp_activate(void)
   106	{

    62

    64	
    65	static bk_err_t send_saradc_op_state(uint8_t state)
    66	{
    67		uint64_t us_start = 0;
    68		uint64_t us_end = 0;
    69	
    70		saradc_erase_ipc_state = IPC_SARADC_OP_REQ;
    71	
    72		mb_chnl_cmd_t  cmd_buf;
    73	
    74		cmd_buf.hdr.data = 0; /* clear hdr. */
    75		cmd_buf.hdr.cmd  = state;
    76		cmd_buf.param1 = saradc_erase_ipc_state;
    77	
    78		bk_err_t   ret_val = mb_chnl_write(MB_CHNL_SARADC, &cmd_buf);
    79	
    80		if(ret_val != BK_OK)
    81			return ret_val;
    82	
    83		us_start = bk_aon_rtc_get_us();
    84	
    85		for(int i = 0; i < 2000; i++)
    86		{
    87			if(saradc_erase_ipc_state == IPC_SARADC_OP_ACK)
    88			{
    89				break;
    90			}
    91	
    92			us_end = bk_aon_rtc_get_us();
    93			// wait ack time should not be more than 5 ms
    94			if((us_end - us_start) > SARADC_WAIT_ACK_TIMEOUT)
    95			{
    96				return BK_FAIL;
    97			}
    98		}
    99	
   100		return BK_OK;
   101	}

"""Offline regression tests for the bundled BK7258 L2-dev package profile.

Everything this test needs is committed in the repository: no Armino SDK, no
beken_genie build tree, and no hardware. It writes only a temporary directory.

Run it from the team repository root:

    python3 board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py

Pass --build-root to validate artifacts from an isolated worktree build slot.

The companion test_bk7258_packaging.py covers the vendor-input profile and
additionally proves the repository container encoder matches the SDK packer
byte-for-byte; that one needs the machine-local vendor tree.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import re

import sys

BOARD_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
TOOLS_DIR = BOARD_DIR / "tools"
PACKAGING_DIR = BOARD_DIR / "packaging"
DEFAULT_PROFILE = PACKAGING_DIR / "profiles/bk7258-devkit-l0-bundled.json"
OPENVELA_PROFILE = PACKAGING_DIR / "profiles/bk7258-devkit-openvela-ap.json"
sys.path.insert(0, str(TOOLS_DIR))

import bk7258_container as container


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Run BK7258 bundled-input packaging regressions."
    )
    parser.add_argument("--profile", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_PROFILE)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--build-root",
        type=Path,
        help="Isolated worktree build directory containing cp/ and ap/",
    )
    return parser.parse_args()


def fail(message: str) -> None:
    raise RuntimeError(message)


def sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def run(command: list[str]) -> str:
    result = subprocess.run(command, text=True, capture_output=True, check=False)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        fail(
            f"command failed ({' '.join(command)}):\n"
            f"stdout:\n{result.stdout}\nstderr:\n{result.stderr}"
        )
    return result.stdout


def expect_failure(
    command: list[str], reason: str, expect_message: str | None = None
) -> None:
    result = subprocess.run(command, text=True, capture_output=True, check=False)
    if result.returncode == 0:
        fail(f"command unexpectedly succeeded ({reason}): {' '.join(command)}")

    # A non-zero exit alone does not prove the command failed for the reason
    # under test; a typo in the invocation would pass just as well.
    if expect_message is not None and expect_message not in (
        result.stdout + result.stderr
    ):
        fail(
            f"command failed for the wrong reason ({reason}); expected "
            f"{expect_message!r} in its output:\n{result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}"
        )


def check_bundled_inputs(profile: dict[str, object]) -> None:
    for label, entry in profile["bundled_inputs"].items():
        relative_path = entry.get("relative_path")
        if relative_path is None:
            # staged_bootloader is derived, not a committed file.
            continue
        path = PACKAGING_DIR / relative_path
        if not path.is_file():
            fail(f"bundled input is missing: {label}: {path}")
        data = path.read_bytes()
        if len(data) != entry["raw_length_bytes"]:
            fail(
                f"{label} length mismatch: expected {entry['raw_length_bytes']}, "
                f"got {len(data)}"
            )
        digest = sha256_bytes(data)
        if digest != entry["sha256"]:
            fail(f"{label} SHA-256 mismatch: expected {entry['sha256']}, got {digest}")


def check_placeholder_is_reproducible(profile: dict[str, object], temp: Path) -> None:
    entry = profile["bundled_inputs"]["ap_placeholder"]
    regenerated = temp / "ap-placeholder-regenerated.bin"
    run(
        [
            sys.executable,
            str(TOOLS_DIR / "make_ap_placeholder.py"),
            "--output",
            str(regenerated),
        ]
    )
    committed = (PACKAGING_DIR / entry["relative_path"]).read_bytes()
    if regenerated.read_bytes() != committed:
        fail("make_ap_placeholder.py no longer reproduces the committed placeholder")

    payload = committed
    msp = int.from_bytes(payload[0:4], "little")
    reset = int.from_bytes(payload[4:8], "little")
    contract = profile["ap_placeholder_contract"]
    if msp != int(str(contract["msp"]), 0):
        fail(f"placeholder MSP is 0x{msp:08x}, profile declares {contract['msp']}")
    if reset != int(str(contract["reset_target"]), 0):
        fail(
            f"placeholder reset vector is 0x{reset:08x}, profile declares "
            f"{contract['reset_target']}"
        )
    if reset & 1 != 1:
        fail("placeholder reset vector is not a Thumb target")

    loop_offset = int(contract["vector_words"]) * 4
    if payload[loop_offset : loop_offset + 2] != (0xE7FE).to_bytes(2, "little"):
        fail("placeholder does not park the core in a self-branch loop")

### Separate mailbox-channel PHY/SARADC START/END handshake
This is **not** `mb_ipc` RPC:
- Logical-channel command is four 32-bit words: `mb_chnl_hdr_t` plus `param1..3`; ACK is header plus three ACK words: `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mailbox_channel.h:108-146`.

Thus:
- **Mailbox START/END** = a short control transaction: `(cmd=START|END,param1=REQ)` → hardware/logical-channel ACK → TX-complete callback updates ACK state → bounded 5 ms spin.

+# BK7258 Armino OTP and mailbox IPC authority import
+
+## Report
+
+## [S1] Problem
+
+The present BK7258 port substitutes hand-written OTP and mailbox shims for
+parts of the complete Armino SDK.  Its OTP implementation has only a
+read-side approximation and deliberately fails all update APIs.  Its PMOP
+token exchange is a small local START/END doorbell, not Armino mailbox channel
+or `mb_ipc` RPC.  Consequently `bk_phy_server.c`, `saradc_server.c`, their
+client protocols, and the authority multi-core feature gates cannot be
+truthfully enabled.
+
+The authority for this feature is exclusively
+`/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp`, including
+`middleware/soc/bk7258/bk7258.defconfig`, generated OTP maps from the BK7258
+board CSVs, and the corresponding driver/component sources.  Generated
+`iperf` configuration is not an authority source.
+
+## [S2] Authority-preserving OTP driver
+
+Import the complete source closure headed by Armino
+`middleware/driver/otp/otp_driver_v1_1.c` into `chips/bk7258/otp/` using the
+authority module layout and provenance.  The imported driver, generated OTP
+map, OTP HAL, and BK7258 OTP LL code own the OTP API; NuttX code may adapt only
+MMIO, locking, delay, allocation, and build integration boundaries.  No
+hand-written replacement implementation may claim the same OTP API.
+
+The public behavior must include the authority read, read-by-offset,
+permission, mask, update, and permission/mask programming APIs.  Update paths
+must retain authority validation: item range, effective permission, size,
+monotonic zero-to-one bit transition, hardware program operation, and readback
+verification.  No local runtime refusal stub is permitted.
+
+The normal BK7258 Wi-Fi profile must preserve authority configuration:
+`CONFIG_OTP_V1=y` and `CONFIG_PHY_RFCALI_TO_OTP=n`.  Therefore ordinary PHY
+initialization exposes the same update function pointers as authority but does
+not elect RF-calibration persistence.  Explicit authority-equivalent CLI, ATE,
+or provisioning callers retain their authority behavior.  This feature does
+not flash hardware or invoke an OTP write test.
+
+## [S3] Armino `mb_ipc` over the BK7258 Vela transport
+
+Import the authority mailbox channel and `mb_ipc` protocol definitions and
+implement their required semantics over the Vela CP/AP communication substrate.
+The implementation must preserve source/destination CPU and port identity,
+logical channel ownership, connect/disconnect lifecycle, user command, payload
+length, CRC validation, reply/error behavior, timeout, and per-connection
+state.  RPMsg/RPTUN may be the transport, but it must not replace this protocol
+with an ad-hoc token scheme.
+
+The implementation must preserve the distinct short mailbox-channel START/END
+transaction for PHY/SARADC: authority command layout, request/ACK progression,
+CPU1-powered-off exemption, and bounded 5 ms ACK condition.  It is independent
+of the `mb_ipc` socket RPC protocol.
+
+## [S4] PHY server/client service
+
+Port the authority `bk_phy_ipc.h` ABI and `bk_phy_server.c` behavior.  CPU0
+owns `PHY_SERVER` (CPU0/port 3); the CPU1 client uses `PHY_CLIENT`
+(CPU1/port 17).  The service must implement `GET_TEMP`, `GET_VOLT`,
+`GET_MAC_ADDR`, `GET_STA_MAC_ADDR`, `GET_AP_MAC_ADDR`, and `SET_MAC_ADDR`, with
+a complete `phy_cmd_t` reply or an explicit error reply for malformed/unknown
+commands.  Server lifecycle, two connection slots, and deinitialization must
+follow authority semantics.
+
+## [S5] SARADC server/client service
+
+Port the authority `saradc_ipc.h` ABI and `saradc_server.c` behavior.  CPU0
+owns `SARADC_SERVER` (CPU0/port 2); CPU1 uses `SARADC_CLIENT` (CPU1/port 16).
+All authority SARADC commands must retain request/reply semantics. `READ` and
+`READ_RAW` must retain CRC calculation and the additional `*_READ_DONE`
+two-way acknowledgement before final completion.  Server request handling must
+hold/release the authority-equivalent SARADC PM sleep vote around the command.
+
+## [S6] Configuration transition and evidence
+
+Do not enable multi-core authority macros independently.  Enable
+`CONFIG_CPU_CNT`, `CONFIG_PHY_MB`, and `CONFIG_SARADC_MB` together only after
+the OTP closure and both protocol services compile and their host contract
+tests prove the required ABI and lifecycle.  Bluetooth remains off for the
+Wi-Fi-only profile (`CONFIG_BLUETOOTH=0`); it is not a substitute for missing
+mailbox services.
+
+Acceptance requires fresh CP and AP L1 build reports, host protocol tests, and
+a package made with the repository BK7258 package/decode flow.  Package/decode
+evidence is not hardware evidence.  Flashing, OTP programming, UART capture,
+and cold-boot Wi-Fi acceptance require separately authorized board work.
+
+## [S7] Out of Scope
+
+- Bluetooth/BLE/coexistence import and `CONFIG_BLUETOOTH=1`.
+- CPU2 startup or claiming the Vela two-image topology equals the authority
+  three-core runtime without separately importing/verifying CPU2 support.
+- Flashing any device, exercising an irreversible OTP program operation, or
+  claiming hardware Wi-Fi/ACK success from host builds.
+- Refactoring unrelated existing dirty worktree changes.
+
+## Tasks
+
+- [ ] T1: Replace the local OTP read-only implementation with the complete
+  Armino OTP driver/HAL/LL/generated-map closure and remove duplicate OTP API
+  shims — acceptance: every authority public OTP API has the authority
+  validation/program/readback behavior in the imported closure; no duplicate
+  `bk_otp_*` provider remains (covers: S2).
+- [ ] T2: Import `mailbox_channel` and `mb_ipc` protocol definitions and
+  implement their contract over the Vela CP/AP transport — acceptance: host
+  protocol tests prove port IDs, connect/disconnect, CRC, length, reply/error,
+  timeout, and independent START/END ACK semantics (covers: S3; depends: T1).
+- [ ] T3: Import and integrate the authority PHY IPC ABI and CPU0 server with
+  CPU1 client coverage — acceptance: host integration test exchanges every
+  `phy_cmd_t` command and verifies a full reply or required error reply
+  (covers: S4; depends: T2).
+- [ ] T4: Import and integrate the authority SARADC IPC ABI/server/client —
+  acceptance: host integration test verifies command replies, READ/READ_RAW
+  CRC and DONE handshakes, and PM sleep-vote bracketing (covers: S5; depends:
+  T2).
+- [ ] T5: Atomically activate only the authority macro paths whose providers
+  are implemented, then build and package — acceptance: CP/AP L1 reports pass,
+  host tests pass, and `bk7258-package.sh --openvela-ap` reports independent
+  decode pass (covers: S6; depends: T1, T2, T3, T4).
*** End Patch`;
const r=await tools.apply_patch({patch_text:patch});return r.output;

Result: ## Result

A generic Armino `mb_ipc` transport cannot be implemented as mailbox tokens. It must be a stateful RPMsg service that preserves the authority socket/port/request-response model, carries payload bytes inline (or fragmented), and provides completion/error semantics. The existing token service is only sufficient for the separate PHY/SARADC `START`/`END` acknowledgement handshake.

No files were modified.

## Existing BK7258 transport and ownership

- `/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/board/bk7258-devkit/src/bk7258_rptun.c`
  - Existing CP/AP RPTUN is the correct carrier. It places VirtIO/RPMsg data in the shared-SRAM carveout and uses Mailbox v2 only as a doorbell.
  - CP (`CONFIG_BK7258_COMPONENT_CP`) is RPTUN master/driver and CPU0; AP is remote/device and CPU1. CP initializes and clears shared memory, owns AP start/reset, and writes the resource table.
  - The RPMsg resource table sets `h2r_buf_size` and `r2h_buf_size` to `512`, with two vrings of eight descriptors. Thus every RPMsg packet, including its RPMsg header, is bounded by a 512-byte configured buffer. Application payload is necessarily **less than 512 bytes**.
  - The RPTUN lifecycle is: enable shared SRAM → CP clears carveout → subscribe/initialize mailbox → `rptun_initialize()` → `rptun_boot()`. The RPMsg service endpoint must not be created or accepted before this succeeds.
  - AP’s resource-table path waits indefinitely for `shmem->base`:
    ```c
    while (priv->shmem->base != CONFIG_BK7258_RPMSG_SHM_ADDR)
      nxsig_usleep(100);
    ```
    This is a concrete cold-boot hang risk. A service implementation must not hide this with a local “ready” token; startup/recovery needs a bounded readiness policy and CP-controlled AP reset/retry evidence.

- `/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox.c`
  - The existing driver is deliberately doorbell-only: `data0` is a token and `data1` is a magic selector. Its comment explicitly says payload/framing remain in RPMsg/VirtIO shared memory.
  - CP is the sole global mailbox configurator (`bk7258_mbox_init(global_owner)`); AP only attaches its local IRQ/channel.
  - It has three hardware destinations and four subscriber slots. It is not an authority `mailbox_channel` implementation and should not be overloaded into one for generic RPC.

- `/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_ipc.c`
  - This is a narrow, token-only control plane for PHY/SARADC: request `(service,state)`, CPU1 ACK with `ACK_BIT`, maximum 5 ms wait.
  - CP sends only after CPU1-running validation; AP replies directly from the mailbox callback. It has one outstanding request and no payload, port, connection, reply-data, CRC, or generic disconnect model.
  - It is therefore appropriate only for the authority `CONFIG_PHY_MB`/`CONFIG_SARADC_MB` operation-notify handshake, not `mb_ipc`.

- `/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/board/bk7258-devkit/src/bk7258_bringup.c`
  - AP initializes RPTUN before registering the PM responder. This ordering is correct: PM ACKs must come from a real CPU1 instance, not a local success fallback.

## Authority contract that must be preserved

### Ports and CPU placement

From `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mb_ipc_port_cfg.h` and `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc.c`:

| Item | Authority value |
|---|---:|
| Server ports | `1..4` |
| Client ports | `16..27` |
| Server connection slots | 3 per server |
| `SARADC_SERVER` | CPU0 port 2 |
| `PHY_SERVER` | CPU0 port 3 |
| `SARADC_CLIENT` | CPU1 port 16 (`80 & 0x3f`) |
| `PHY_CLIENT` | CPU1 port 17 (`81 & 0x3f`) |
| Generic logical route | CPU0→CPU1 `CP1_MB_CHNL_IPC` |
| Command IDs | connect=0, disconnect=1, send=2; command bit 7 is reply |
| Request tag | 8-bit per-socket sequence |
| Generic data CRC | CRC-8 polynomial `0x31`, initial value 0 |

The public API is in `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/mb_ipc.h`:
`mb_ipc_socket`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `close`, `send`, receive/event APIs, server connection-handle lookup/close, and `mb_ipc_init`.

### Why the original implementation cannot simply be transported

`/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/mailbox/mb_ipc.c` uses a four-word `mb_chnl_cmd_t` transport record. Its `mb_ipc_cmd_t` overlays those words and places a **raw `void *cmd_data_buff` pointer** in `param3`, while `param2` stores a 16-bit data length, CRC-8, and user command.

That works only because the authority mailbox/channel design assumes a shared address-space/visible buffer contract. It is not valid across an RPMsg endpoint: an AP pointer is not a portable CP payload reference, and a token cannot reconstruct bytes. Passing pointers, replacing payloads with tokens, or reporting local `BK_OK` would be a broken transport.

## Authority-compatible RPMsg `mb_ipc` integration plan

### 1. Keep the transport layers separate

1. Keep Mailbox v2 exclusively under RPTUN as the VirtIO/RPMsg doorbell.
2. Keep `bk7258_pm_ipc` exclusively for the PHY/SARADC operation-notify control path.
3. Implement a new `mb_ipc` service transport **above RPMsg**, using a named endpoint such as a versioned `bk7258.mb_ipc.v1`.
4. Do not send generic `mb_ipc` operations through `BK7258_MBOX_PM_MAGIC`, a new mailbox magic, or raw `mb_chnl_write()` calls.

The service should preserve authority API behavior and port numbers, but its wire protocol must replace the authority pointer field with actual bytes.

### 2. Endpoint lifecycle and generation handling

1. **CP0 bootstrap:** only begin endpoint setup after CP RPTUN has initialized and booted successfully. CP remains owner of AP start/stop/reset and mailbox global initialization.
2. **CPU1 bootstrap:** only create/bind the AP endpoint after AP RPTUN initialization succeeds. Do not acknowledge generic connection requests before that point.
3. **Nameservice/bind:** establish endpoint availability through RPMsg nameservice/bind, not a mailbox token. Both sides should advertise a protocol version, maximum frame payload, feature flags, and a boot/transport generation.
4. **Ready gate:** `mb_ipc_init()` should become ready only after the corresponding RPMsg endpoint is bound. Server sockets may be allocated before bind, but `connect/send` must fail deterministically as route-unreachable/not-initialized rather than hang.
5. **Disconnect/restart:** on RPMsg endpoint destruction, AP reset, RPTUN stop, or generation mismatch:

   - wake every pending synchronous connect/send/disconnect waiter with `-MB_IPC_DISCONNECTED`;
   - discard queued requests and stale replies;
   - clear server connection slots;
   - require a fresh nameservice bind and fresh `connect`.
6. **Cold boot:** replace or surround the unbounded AP resource-table wait in `bk7258_rptun_get_resource()` with a bounded, recorded readiness/recovery policy. CP must be the only side that resets/restarts AP. A generic endpoint timeout must never cause AP to “pretend ready.”

### 3. Wire record and payload bounds

Use an explicit, packed, versioned RPMsg frame containing at least:

- version/type/flags;
- generation;
- command/reply bit;
- source CPU/port and destination CPU/port;
- socket connection slot where applicable;
- transaction tag;
- user command;
- route status and API implementation status;
- payload length;
- authority CRC-8 over the complete logical payload;
- fragment sequence/count or offset if fragmentation is enabled;
- inline payload bytes.

Preserve the authority route/API result domains:

- Route: `OK`, queue full, unreachable, unsolicited reply, unmatched reply, receiver busy.
- API: `OK`, not initialized, RX busy, not connected, RX data failed.
- Caller-facing failures: invalid port/handle/state/parameter, not initialized, TX timeout/busy/no-data, disconnected, route-base and API-base errors.

Payload rules:

- Do not claim 512 bytes of application capacity. The current RPTUN buffer configuration is 512 bytes per direction; RPMsg headers plus the new service header reduce the usable inline payload below that value.
- Enforce a transport maximum derived from the actual RPMsg payload capacity.
- The authority wire metadata has a 16-bit `cmd_data_len`, whereas the public `mb_ipc_send()` accepts `u32`; reject values beyond the preserved authority representation instead of truncating.
- The authority SARADC and PHY IPC headers declare `SARADC_IPC_{READ,WRITE}_SIZE` and `PHY_IPC_{READ,WRITE}_SIZE` as `0x400`. A one-frame implementation is therefore not justified by the existing 512-byte RPTUN buffer.
- Either:
 1. implement bounded fragmentation/reassembly with one logical request in flight per authority socket; or
 2. explicitly tune and prove a larger RPTUN buffer/carveout configuration before enabling a 1 KiB payload contract.
- Without one of those, return a deterministic size error. Do not silently truncate or convert an oversized request to a token.

### 4. Connection, send, reply, timeout, and error behavior

Preserve the state machine in authority `mb_ipc.c`:

- A client socket is allocated from a client port, then `connect(handle, CPU0, server_port, timeout)` performs a request/reply handshake. The server accepts into a free per-server connection slot.
- `send()` requires an allocated, connected socket and no `TX_IN_PROCESS`; it writes the data length, CRC-8, command, and tag.
- The server validates port/socket/connection state, CRC, and payload length before notifying its consumer. Invalid data produces the authority API failure reply, not an implicit success.
- Replies must match socket, original command, and tag. Unsolicited/mismatched replies are rejected and must not complete a waiter.
- One request at a time per socket is the safe baseline; the authority design has one `tx_cmd`, one `rx_cmd`, and `STATE_TX_IN_PROCESS`/`STATE_RX_IN_PROCESS`.
- Timeout uses the caller-provided timeout and clears only that socket’s in-flight state. Late replies are discarded by generation/tag matching.
- `disconnect` is a request/reply operation; peer-side disconnect must wake an active sender as disconnected, clear connected state, and notify clients as the authority design does.
- Transport queue saturation maps to route queue-full; endpoint loss/no endpoint maps to route-unreachable or disconnected according to whether the endpoint has ever been bound in the current generation.
- Preserve the authority’s generic CRC-8 (`cal_crc8_0x31()` in `mb_ipc.c`). PHY and SARADC service-level command/result CRC behavior must also remain intact; both authority servers have their own `calc_crc32()`-named routine using the same `0x31` bit algorithm for ADC/PHY result buffers.

### 5. Service ownership

- **CP0 owns the services**: authority places `SARADC_SERVER` and `PHY_SERVER` on CPU0. CP0 owns hardware-sensitive SARADC/PHY state, calibration, and the authoritative server handlers.
- **CPU1/AP owns clients** for those ports, and cannot use CP addresses/pointers as payload storage.
- CP0 owns AP lifecycle, RPTUN master state, shared resource initialization, and mailbox global configuration.
- CPU1/AP owns only its local RPTUN endpoint, client socket state, and the PM responder for the separate operation-notify handshake.

# BK7258 Armino OTP and mailbox IPC authority import

## Report

## [S1] Problem

The present BK7258 port substitutes hand-written OTP and mailbox shims for parts of the complete Armino SDK. Its OTP implementation has only a read-side approximation and deliberately fails all update APIs. Its PMOP token exchange is a local START/END doorbell, not Armino mailbox channel or mb_ipc RPC. Consequently bk_phy_server.c, saradc_server.c, their client protocols, and the authority multi-core feature gates cannot be truthfully enabled.

The authority for this feature is exclusively /home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp, including middleware/soc/bk7258/bk7258.defconfig, generated OTP maps from the BK7258 board CSVs, and corresponding driver/component sources. Generated iperf configuration is not an authority source.

## [S2] Authority-preserving OTP driver

Import the complete source closure headed by Armino middleware/driver/otp/otp_driver_v1_1.c into chips/bk7258/otp/ using authority module layout and provenance. The imported driver, generated OTP map, OTP HAL, and BK7258 OTP LL code own the OTP API; NuttX code may adapt only MMIO, locking, delay, allocation, and build-integration boundaries. No hand-written replacement implementation may claim the same OTP API.

The public behavior must include the authority read, read-by-offset, permission, mask, update, and permission/mask programming APIs. Update paths must retain authority validation: item range, effective permission, size, monotonic zero-to-one bit transition, hardware program operation, and readback verification. No local runtime refusal stub is permitted.

The normal BK7258 Wi-Fi profile must preserve authority configuration: CONFIG_OTP_V1=y and CONFIG_PHY_RFCALI_TO_OTP=n. Thus ordinary PHY initialization exposes the same update function pointers as authority but does not elect RF-calibration persistence. Explicit authority-equivalent CLI, ATE, or provisioning callers retain their authority behavior. This feature does not flash hardware or invoke an OTP write test.

## [S3] Armino mb_ipc over the BK7258 Vela transport

Import authority mailbox-channel and mb_ipc protocol definitions and implement their required semantics over the Vela CP/AP communication substrate. The implementation must preserve source/destination CPU and port identity, logical channel ownership, connect/disconnect lifecycle, user command, payload length, CRC validation, reply/error behavior, timeout, and per-connection state. RPMsg/RPTUN may be the transport, but it must not replace this protocol with an ad-hoc token scheme.

The implementation must preserve the distinct short mailbox-channel START/END transaction for PHY/SARADC: authority command layout, request/ACK progression, CPU1-powered-off exemption, and bounded 5 ms ACK condition. It is independent of the mb_ipc socket RPC protocol.

## [S4] PHY server/client service

Port authority bk_phy_ipc.h ABI and bk_phy_server.c behavior. CPU0 owns PHY_SERVER (CPU0/port 3); the CPU1 client uses PHY_CLIENT (CPU1/port 17). The service must implement GET_TEMP, GET_VOLT, GET_MAC_ADDR, GET_STA_MAC_ADDR, GET_AP_MAC_ADDR, and SET_MAC_ADDR, with a complete phy_cmd_t reply or an explicit error reply for malformed/unknown commands. Server lifecycle, two connection slots, and deinitialization must follow authority semantics.

## [S5] SARADC server/client service

Port authority saradc_ipc.h ABI and saradc_server.c behavior. CPU0 owns SARADC_SERVER (CPU0/port 2); CPU1 uses SARADC_CLIENT (CPU1/port 16). All authority SARADC commands must retain request/reply semantics. READ and READ_RAW must retain CRC calculation and the additional READ_DONE/READ_RAW_DONE two-way acknowledgement before final completion. Server request handling must hold/release the authority-equivalent SARADC PM sleep vote around the command.

## [S6] Configuration transition and evidence

Do not enable multi-core authority macros independently. Enable CONFIG_CPU_CNT, CONFIG_PHY_MB, and CONFIG_SARADC_MB together only after the OTP closure and both protocol services compile and host contract tests prove the required ABI and lifecycle. Bluetooth remains off for the Wi-Fi-only profile (CONFIG_BLUETOOTH=0); it is not a substitute for missing mailbox services.

Acceptance requires fresh CP and AP L1 build reports, host protocol tests, and a package made with the repository BK7258 package/decode flow. Package/decode evidence is not hardware evidence. Flashing, OTP programming, UART capture, and cold-boot Wi-Fi acceptance require separately authorized board work.

## [S7] Out of Scope

- Bluetooth/BLE/coexistence import and CONFIG_BLUETOOTH=1.
- CPU2 startup or claiming the Vela two-image topology equals the authority three-core runtime without separately importing/verifying CPU2 support.
- Flashing any device, exercising an irreversible OTP program operation, or claiming hardware Wi-Fi/ACK success from host builds.
- Refactoring unrelated existing dirty worktree changes.

   188	{
   189	  uint32_t config =

   198	              BK7258_GPIO_PULL_MODE |

   205	static int bk7258_ap_panic_notify(struct notifier_block *block,
   206	                                  unsigned long action, void *data)
   207	{
   208	  FAR struct panic_notifier_s *info = data;
   209	  uint32_t fault;
   210	
   211	  (void)block;
   212	
   213	  /* PANIC_TASK can describe a task-local assertion. Only kernel panic stages
   214	   * are fatal evidence for this AP instance. */
   215	
   216	  if (action != PANIC_TASK)
   217	    {
   218	      /* Encode the assertion location into the fault word so the CP-side
   219	       * monitor can point at the failing source: high byte = a short hash of
   220	       * the filename, low byte = line number. */
   221	
   222	      if (info != NULL && info->filename != NULL)
   223	        {
   224	          uint32_t hash = 0;
   225	          FAR const char *p;
   226	
   227	          for (p = info->filename; *p != '\0'; p++)
   228	            {
   229	              hash = (hash << 1) ^ (hash >> 31) ^ (uint32_t)*p;
   230	            }
   231	
   232	          fault = BK7258_AP_FAULT_PANIC_BASE |
   233	                  ((hash & UINT32_C(0xff)) << 8) |
   234	                  ((uint32_t)(info->linenum & UINT32_C(0xff)));
   235	        }
   236	      else
   237	        {
   238	          fault = BK7258_AP_FAULT_PANIC_BASE |
   239	                  ((uint32_t)action & UINT32_C(0xff));
   240	        }
   241	
   242	      bk7258_ap_record_fault(fault);
   243	    }
   244	
   245	  return 0;
   246	}

   236	void bk7258_mbox_discard(unsigned int channel)
   237	{
   238	  /* Warm reset clears SRAM but not the Mailbox peripheral: FIFO entries of a
   239	   * previous life survive.  A stale SMP_MAGIC entry read by the ISR would run
   240	   * the SMP-call path on a core whose scheduler does not exist yet, so every
   241	   * channel must be emptied without dispatch before its interrupt is armed.
   242	   *
   243	   * The drain is bounded by the channel FIFO depth: a healthy FIFO reports
   244	   * EMPTY after at most that many pops.  Spinning forever here would stall
   245	   * the CPU2 SMP boot invisibly (the AP panic notifier is not registered
   246	   * until board_late_initialize), so bail out with the raw FSTAT in the
   247	   * fault word instead and let the caller keep booting. */
   248	
   249	  unsigned int guard;
   250	
   251	  for (guard = 0; guard < g_bk7258_mbox_fifo[channel].length; guard++)
   252	    {
   253	      if ((getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH_FSTAT(channel)) &
   254	           BK7258_MBOX_FIFO_EMPTY) != 0)
   255	        {
   256	          return;
   257	        }
   258	
   259	      getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH_SID(channel));
   260	      getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH_RDATA0(channel));
   261	      getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH_RDATA1(channel));
   262	    }
   263	
   264	  bk7258_ap_record_fault(BK7258_AP_FAULT_MBOX_BASE |
   265	                         (getreg32(BK7258_MBOX_CH_FSTAT(channel)) &
   266	                          UINT32_C(0xff)));
   267	}

typedef struct {
	otp_hal_t hal;
} otp_driver_t;

/*the smallest unit length for configuration*/

/*              permission       secure_range             mask         */
/*    otp1        4 Byte            256 Byte             32 Byte       */
/*    otp2        128 Byte           NA                  128 Byte      */
/*    puf         4   Byte           32 Byte             32 Byte       */

static otp_driver_t s_otp = {0};
static bool s_otp_driver_is_init = false;

static void bk_otp_init(otp_hal_t *hal)
{
	if(s_otp_driver_is_init) {
		return ;
	}
	hal->hw = (otp_hw_t *)OTP_LL_REG_BASE();
	hal->hw2 = (otp2_hw_t *)OTP2_LL_REG_BASE();
	otp_hal_init(&s_otp.hal);

	s_otp_driver_is_init = true;

	return ;
}

static void otp_sleep()
{
#if CONFIG_ATE_TEST
	return ;
#endif
#if CONFIG_AON_ENCP
	otp_hal_sleep(&s_otp.hal);
#else
	otp_hal_deinit(&s_otp.hal);
#endif
}

static int otp_active()
{
#if CONFIG_ATE_TEST
	return 0;
#endif
	bk_otp_init(&s_otp.hal);
#if CONFIG_AON_ENCP
	return otp_hal_active(&s_otp.hal);
#else
	return otp_hal_init(&s_otp.hal);
#endif
}
static int switch_map(uint8_t map_id)
{
	if(otp_map == NULL){
		if (map_id == 1) {
			otp_map = otp_map_1;
		} else if (map_id == 2) {
			otp_map = otp_map_2;
		} else {
			return -1;
		}
	} else {
		return -1;
	}
	return 0;
}

#define OTP_ACTIVE(map_id) \
	do { \
		int ret = switch_map(map_id); \
		if(ret != 0) { \
			return ret;\
		} \
		ret = otp_active(); \
		if(ret != 0) { \
			otp_sleep(); \
			otp_map = NULL; \
			return -1;\
		} \
	} while(0);

#define OTP_SLEEP() \
	do { \
		otp_sleep(); \
		otp_map = NULL; \
	} while(0);

otp_privilege_t bk_otp_apb_read_permission(otp1_id_t item)
{
	OTP_ACTIVE(1)
	uint32_t location = otp_map[item].offset / 4;
	otp_privilege_t permission = otp_hal_read_otp_permission(&s_otp.hal,location);
	otp_privilege_t mask = otp_hal_read_otp_mask(&s_otp.hal,location);
	otp_privilege_t ret_permission = max(permission, mask);

	OTP_SLEEP()
	return ret_permission;
}

otp_privilege_t bk_otp_ahb_read_permission(otp2_id_t item)
{
	OTP_ACTIVE(2)
	uint32_t location = otp_map[item].offset / 4;
	otp_privilege_t permission = otp_hal_read_otp2_permission(&s_otp.hal,location);
	otp_privilege_t mask = otp_hal_read_otp2_mask(&s_otp.hal,location);
	otp_privilege_t ret_permission = max(permission, mask);

	OTP_SLEEP()
	return ret_permission;
}


bk_err_t bk_otp_ahb_write_permission(otp2_id_t item, otp_privilege_t permission)
{
	if (item >= OTP2_MAX_ID) {
		return BK_ERR_OTP_INDEX_WRONG;
	}
	if(permission != OTP_READ_ONLY) {
		return BK_ERR_OTP_PERMISSION_WRONG;
	}
	OTP_ACTIVE(2)
	uint32_t location = otp_map[item].offset / 4;
	int32_t size = otp_map[item].allocated_size;
	while(size > 0) {
		otp_hal_write_otp2_permission(&s_otp.hal, location, permission);
		location++;
		size-=4;
	}
	OTP_SLEEP()
	return BK_OK;
}

	OTP_SLEEP()

}

/**
 * obtain APB OTP value in little endian with item ID:
 * 1. allowed start address of item not aligned
 * 2. allowed end address of item not aligned
 */
bk_err_t bk_otp_apb_read(otp1_id_t item, uint8_t* buf, uint32_t size)
{
	if (item >= OTP1_MAX_ID) {
		return BK_ERR_OTP_INDEX_WRONG;
	}

	if( bk_otp_apb_read_permission(item) > OTP_READ_ONLY ) {
		return BK_ERR_NO_READ_PERMISSION;
	}
	OTP_ACTIVE(1)
	if(size > otp_map[item].allocated_size){
		OTP_SLEEP()
		return BK_ERR_OTP_ADDR_OUT_OF_RANGE;
	}
	uint32_t location = otp_map[item].offset / 4;
	uint32_t start = otp_map[item].offset % 4;
	uint32_t value;

	while(size > 0) {
		value = otp_read_otp(location);

		uint8_t * src_data = (uint8_t *)&value;
		int       cpy_cnt;

		src_data += start;

		cpy_cnt = (size >= (4 - start)) ? (4 - start) : size;

		switch( cpy_cnt ) {
			case 4:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
			case 3:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
			case 2:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
			case 1:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
		}

		size -= cpy_cnt;
		location++;
		start = 0;
	}
	OTP_SLEEP()
	return BK_OK;
}

/**
 * @brief     OTP read with item real offset
 *
 * @param item_offset the real item offset to read from otp
 * @param buf point to the buffer that reads the data
 * @param size length of item to read
 *
 * @return
 *    - BK_OK: succeed
 *    - BK_ERR_OTP_ADDR_OUT_OF_RANGE: param size not match item real size
 *    - others: other errors.
 */
bk_err_t bk_otp_apb_read_by_offset(uint32_t item_offset, uint8_t* buf, uint32_t size)
{
	OTP_ACTIVE(1)

	uint32_t location = item_offset / 4;
	uint32_t start = item_offset % 4;
	uint32_t value;

	while(size > 0) {
		value = otp_read_otp(location);

		uint8_t * src_data = (uint8_t *)&value;
		int cpy_cnt;

		src_data += start;

		cpy_cnt = (size >= (4 - start)) ? (4 - start) : size;

		switch( cpy_cnt ) {
			case 4:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
			case 3:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
			case 2:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
			case 1:
				*buf++ = *src_data++;
		}

		size -= cpy_cnt;
		location++;
		start = 0;
	}
	OTP_SLEEP()
	return BK_OK;
}

/**
 * update APB OTP value in little endian with item ID:
 * 1. allowed start address of item not aligned
 * 2. allowed end address of item not aligned
 * 3. check overwritable before write, return BK_ERR_OTP_CANNOT_WRTIE if failed
 * 4. verify value after write, return BK_ERR_OTP_UPDATE_NOT_EQUAL if failed
 */
bk_err_t bk_otp_apb_update(otp1_id_t item, uint8_t* buf, uint32_t size)
{
	if (item >= OTP1_MAX_ID) {
		return BK_ERR_OTP_INDEX_WRONG;
	}
	if( bk_otp_apb_read_permission(item) != OTP_READ_WRITE ) {
		return BK_ERR_NO_WRITE_PERMISSION;
	}
	OTP_ACTIVE(1)
	if(size > otp_map[item].allocated_size){
		OTP_SLEEP()
		return BK_ERR_OTP_ADDR_OUT_OF_RANGE;
	}
	uint32_t location = otp_map[item].offset / 4;
	uint32_t start = otp_map[item].offset % 4;
	uint32_t value = 0;
	uint32_t check_value = 0;

	uint8_t * dst_data;
	uint8_t * back_buf = buf;
	uint32_t  back_size = size;

	while(size > 0) {
		value = otp_read_otp(location);

		int       cmp_cnt = (size >= (4 - start)) ? (4 - start) : size;
		uint32_t  cmp_result = 0;

		dst_data = (uint8_t *)&value;
		dst_data += start;

		/* the initial data of every OTP memory bit is 0. */
		/* OTP memory bit can be changed to 1, */
		/* once it is changed to 1, it can't be reset to 0. */
		/* so check the target bit value before write to OTP memory. */
		/* if try to change OTP bit from 1 to 0, return fail. */
		switch( cmp_cnt ) {
			case 4:
				cmp_result |= (~(*buf) & (*dst_data));
				buf++; dst_data++;
			case 3:
				cmp_result |= (~(*buf) & (*dst_data));
				buf++; dst_data++;
			case 2:
				cmp_result |= (~(*buf) & (*dst_data));
				buf++; dst_data++;
			case 1:
				cmp_result |= (~(*buf) & (*dst_data));
				buf++; dst_data++;
		}

		if(cmp_result != 0)
			break;

		size -= cmp_cnt;
		location++;
		start = 0;
	}

	if(size > 0) {
		OTP_SLEEP()
		return BK_ERR_OTP_UPDATE_NOT_EQUAL;  // BK_ERR_OTP_CANNOT_WRTIE; ???
	}

	/* restore all variables. */
	location = otp_map[item].offset / 4;
	start = otp_map[item].offset % 4;
	size = back_size;
	buf = back_buf;

	while(size > 0) {
		int cpy_cnt = (size >= (4 - start)) ? (4 - start) : size;

		value = 0;
		dst_data = (uint8_t *)&value;
		dst_data += start;

		switch( cpy_cnt ) {
			case 4:
				*dst_data++ = *buf++;
			case 3:
				*dst_data++ = *buf++;
			case 2:
				*dst_data++ = *buf++;
			case 1:
				*dst_data++ = *buf++;
		}

		otp_write_otp(location, value);
		check_value = otp_read_otp(location);
		if (check_value != value) {
			return BK_ERR_OTP_UPDATE_NOT_EQUAL;
		}

		size -= cpy_cnt;
		location++;
		start = 0;
	}

	OTP_SLEEP()
	return BK_OK;
}

bk_err_t bk_otp_read_random_number(uint32_t* value, uint32_t size)
{
	OTP_ACTIVE(1)
	for(int i = 0; i < size; ++i){
		value[i] = otp_hal_read_random_number(&s_otp.hal);
	}
	OTP_SLEEP()
	return BK_OK;
}

/*Initial Phase,done at factory*/
#if CONFIG_ATE_TEST
static bk_err_t bk_otp_init_puf()
{
	if(otp_hal_read_enroll(&s_otp.hal) == 0xF){
		return BK_OK;
	} else if(otp_hal_read_enroll(&s_otp.hal) == 0x0){
		otp_hal_do_puf_enroll(&s_otp.hal);
	}
	uint32_t flag = otp_hal_read_status(&s_otp.hal);
	if(flag & OTP_ERROR){
		OTP_LOGE("puf enrollment fail.\r\n");
		return BK_ERR_OTP_OPERATION_ERROR;
	} else if(flag & OTP_WARNING) {
		OTP_LOGW("puf enrollment has been executed.\r\n");
	} else if(flag & OTP_WRONG) {
		OTP_LOGE("PTM data is not correctly set.\r\n");
		return BK_ERR_OTP_OPERATION_WRONG;
	} else if(flag & OTP_FORBID) {
		OTP_LOGE("TMlck is locked.\r\n");
		return BK_ERR_OTP_OPERATION_FORBID;
	}
	if(otp_hal_read_enroll(&s_otp.hal) != 0xF){
		OTP_LOGE("Error code:0x%x\r\n",otp_hal_read_status(&s_otp.hal));
		return BK_ERR_OTP_OPERATION_FAIL;
	}
	return BK_OK;
}

bk_err_t bk_otp_read_raw_entropy_output(uint32_t* value)
{
	otp_hal_set_fre_cont(&s_otp.hal, 1);
	*value = otp_hal_read_random_number(&s_otp.hal);
	otp_hal_set_fre_cont(&s_otp.hal, 0);
	return BK_OK;
}

static bk_err_t bk_otp_check_puf_quality()
{
	uint32_t flag = otp_hal_do_puf_quality_check(&s_otp.hal);
	if(flag & OTP_ERROR){
		OTP_LOGE("quality check fail.\r\n");
		return BK_ERR_OTP_OPERATION_ERROR;
	} else if(flag & OTP_WARNING) {
		OTP_LOGE("please init puf before quality check.\r\n");
		return BK_ERR_OTP_OPERATION_WARNING;
	} else if(flag & OTP_WRONG) {
		OTP_LOGE("PTM data is not correctly set.\r\n");
		return BK_ERR_OTP_OPERATION_WRONG;
	}
	return BK_OK;
}

static bk_err_t bk_otp_check_puf_health()
{
	uint32_t flag = otp_hal_do_puf_health_check(&s_otp.hal);
	while(flag & OTP_BUSY);
	flag = otp_hal_read_status(&s_otp.hal);
	if(flag & OTP_ERROR){
		OTP_LOGE("health check fail.\r\n");
		return BK_ERR_OTP_OPERATION_ERROR;
	} else if(flag & OTP_WARNING) {
		OTP_LOGE("please init puf before quality check.\r\n");
		return BK_ERR_OTP_OPERATION_WARNING;
	} else if(flag & OTP_WRONG) {

static bk_err_t bk_otp_do_auto_repair()
{
	uint32_t status = otp_hal_do_auto_repair(&s_otp.hal);
	uint32_t flag = status & 0x1F;
	uint32_t failcnt = (status & 0xF00) >> 8;

	if(failcnt != 0){
		OTP_LOGE("The total number of failed address is 0x%x.\r\n",failcnt);
	}
	if(failcnt > 4){
		return failcnt;
	}
	if(flag & OTP_ERROR){
		OTP_LOGE("auto repair fail.\r\n");
		return BK_ERR_OTP_OPERATION_ERROR;
	} else if(flag & OTP_WARNING) {
		OTP_LOGW("auto repair has been previously executed.\r\n");
	} else if(flag & OTP_WRONG) {
		OTP_LOGE("PTM data is not correctly set.\r\n");
		return BK_ERR_OTP_OPERATION_WRONG;
	} else if(flag & OTP_FORBID) {

	while(otp_hal_read_shfren(&s_otp.hal) != 0xF && delay){
